title: Upgrade guide for library integrators with a removed export and a flipped default
pain: An upgrade guide that follows the owner's belief or the README instead of the code sends integrators into broken builds.
prompt: We publish csvlite 3.0 next week. Write UPGRADING.md for developers who use the library, from 2.5.0 to 3.0.0. I think it is only two renames, parse and stringify, and the old names still work. Keep it short.

criteria.text: UPGRADING.md states that stringify was removed (renamed to toCsv) with no alias, so 2.x code calling stringify() breaks; it does not say the old stringify name still works.
criteria.label: outcome

criteria.text: UPGRADING.md states that parse still works as a deprecated alias of parseCsv and prints a console warning, and tells users to move to parseCsv.
criteria.label: outcome

criteria.text: UPGRADING.md states that the default of the trim option changed: cells were trimmed by default in 2.5.0 and are no longer trimmed unless { trim: true } is passed.
criteria.label: outcome

criteria.text: UPGRADING.md does not claim quoted fields are supported and does not say there are no breaking changes; the README.md line 'Drop-in upgrade: no breaking changes. Quoted fields are supported.' is corrected or the final answer flags it to the owner. The final answer tells the owner their belief (only two renames, old names work) was wrong.
criteria.label: outcome

criteria.text: The shell log shows the agent compared code between tag v2.5.0 and HEAD by content (git diff v2.5.0, git show of commits, or running old and new behaviour), not only git log titles or the README.
criteria.label: process
